title: apistore maxAllowedVersion cap must check the persisted encoded version, not the declared one
answers: version cap / maxAllowedVersion bypassed when a serializer or codec upconverts the stored version
how is the storage version cap enforced in apistore
write stored at a version above the configured maximum despite the request declaring a lower one
rejected write still leaves a payload behind
body:
Symptom: a write whose declared version is under the group's configured max-allowed version still ends up persisted above the cap (or an over-cap write isn't rejected) because a codec/serializer silently converted to a different storage version.
Root cause: checking the object's declared version instead of the bytes actually written lets any encoder/serializer that up-converts slip past the cap - pkg/storage/unified/apistore/prepare.go:Storage.encode / persistedVersion.
Fix pattern: encode first, then derive the group/version to check from the encoded JSON via persistedVersion; reject (never rewrite, return nil raw) if that version exceeds the cap or if its group differs from the resource's own group (which can't be ranked and would otherwise slip through unregistered).
Constraints: enforcement only applies when `enforceCap=true` and `VersionPolicy.HasMaxAllowed(group)` is true; deletion-related updates pass `enforceCap=false` deliberately so an already-over-cap object stays removable (drain-only policy). Applies to any custom Serializer plugged into apistore, not just the default codec.
applies: pkg/storage/unified/apistore writes going through Storage.encode, including custom Serializer implementations
